name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes better than generic upscalers, giving EXCAVA a measurable edge in output quality without extra compute. The trade-off is a slight slowdown from the depth estimation step, but the 0.5%+ quality gain justifies it.

name: Torque
text: Depth-aware upscalers won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem is the FO’s face module alone—adding a depth step just masks symptoms, not the single-point failure. Instead, test a fresh face reconstruction model (e.g., RealVisXL’s latest) against the current FO module; if it cuts face errors by 0.5%+, adopt it—no depth upscaler needed.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s latest face reconstruction model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It cuts face fidelity loss by replacing the FO module with a model trained on higher-resolution, cleaner face data—directly attacking the single-point failure Torque flagged. The trade-off is a 1-2% speed hit from the heavier model, but the face quality jump outweighs it.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model risks locking us into another single-point failure—its training data may bias toward certain demographics or lighting, and EXCAVA’s pipeline still won’t know if the face module fails downstream. Test against a fallback ensemble: pair RealVisXL with a lightweight face enhancer (e.g., GFPGAN 2.0) and measure face fidelity *and* pipeline stability—if the ensemble drops below current performance, the "upgrade" fails.
